title: Doctorant(e) "Développement et caractérisation d’une plateforme multi-capteurs pour le monitoring de sites de stockage onshore de CO2" - Contrat doctoral
description:
ENGLISH VERSION

Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c’est s’engager dans une institution où la science et l’innovation bâtissent un avenir plus durable. Une école d’excellence où chacun a l’opportunité de révéler son plein potentiel et de contribuer à relever les défis de demain.

Classée parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France et reconnue mondialement, notre école, membre de l’Institut Mines-Télécom, forme les talents de demain tout en contribuant activement à relever les grands défis industriels, numériques et environnementaux. Avec nous, vous intégrez une communauté de 500 collaborateurs, 2500 étudiants, et participez à un projet ambitieux : conjuguer excellence académique, recherche d’avant-garde et impact sociétal positif.

L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Avec ses 8 Grandes Écoles publiques et 2 écoles filiales, il est le premier institut public dédié aux ingénieurs et managers. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain.

À Mines Saint-Étienne, nos centres de recherche sont le cœur battant de notre École.

Pensés comme de véritables hubs d’innovation, nos cinq Centres de Formation et de Recherche articulent leurs expertises autour de grands enjeux industriels, environnementaux, sociétaux et technologiques.

Leur mission ? Imaginer le monde de demain en alliant excellence académique et impact concret.

Vous rêvez d’une industrie propre, efficace et durable ? Le centre SPIN en fait sa priorité.

Énergie, environnement, procédés industriels… on y conçoit des systèmes pour produire mieux, avec moins.

L’objectif ? Limiter l’impact environnemental, réduire la consommation énergétique et booster l’efficacité.

🔧 Dans un monde en pleine mutation, nos équipes déploient leur créativité scientifique pour accompagner l’industrie du futur. 

Et vous, prêt·e à innover à nos côtés ?

🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vous

En tant que doctorant, vous êtes au cœur de nos missions de recherche et innovation et, dans une moindre mesure de nos missions d’enseignement. Vous serez affecté au centre SPIN – LGF (Laboratoire Georges Friedel, UMR CNRS 5307). Au sein de ce centre, vous conjuguez passion scientifique et impact sociétal.

Le centre SPIN (Science des Procédés Industriels et Naturels), qui sera fortement impliqué dans la thèse, développe, au sein de Mines Saint-Etienne, son expertise dans le domaine du Génie des Procédés appliqué aux systèmes dispersés : grains, particules, gouttes, bulles, milieux poreux. Il possède également des compétences en développement de capteurs et d’instrumentation.

Les technologies de captage et stockage du CO2 sont des technologies clés pour la décarbonation du secteur industriel. Les stockages offshores ont déjà démontré leur faisabilité, mais les stockages onshores semblent nécessaires pour augmenter les capacités de stockage tout en réduisant le transport de CO2. Or, la proximité de ces sites avec les populations rend leurs déploiements incertains et soulève des questions relatives à l’acceptabilité sociale.

La surveillance à long terme des sites de stockage de CO2, exigée par la directive européenne CCS, constitue une opportunité pour renforcer la transparence et l’acceptation locale du stockage en engageant les parties prenantes dans l’acquisition et l’interprétation des données. Cependant, les systèmes actuels de surveillance ne permettent pas à la fois de réaliser des mesures in-situ, simulations numériques et visualisation interactive pour une approche du suivi intégrée des sites de stockage. Le projet CO2MET vise à développer et faire progresser des unités ou éléments clés pour préparer un futur système intégré de surveillance numérique à long terme améliorant la fiabilité et l’acceptabilité du stockage géologique de CO2.

Pour atteindre ces objectifs, le consortium CO2MET a été constitué et est composé de l'IFPEN, du BRGM, de Mines Saint-Etienne et de Cerema.

La surveillance à long terme nécessite des outils fiables et performants, notamment dans le domaine des capteurs environnementaux, ce qui soulève la question de la mise en œuvre de mesures correctives pour traiter le signal, ainsi que celle de l'influence des variations à long terme des paramètres externes sur la réponse des capteurs (et de l'impact du changement climatique). Étant donné que les signaux de concentration en CO₂ peuvent, à eux seuls, ne pas être suffisamment discriminants (les concentrations biologiques dans les sols pouvant dépasser 10 % vol.), compte tenu de leurs origines diverses (sources profondes, provenant du stockage ou de l’interaction gaz-roche ; processus de respiration ; oxydation du méthane), la prévention des faux positifs dans la surveillance des sites de stockage doit s'appuyer sur des capteurs de CO₂ (NDIR ou photoacoustiques) et sur d'autres capteurs (par exemple, un capteur chimique d'O₂), ainsi que sur des capteurs environnementaux (humidité, pression, température) afin de permettre une attribution correcte de la source de CO2.

Parmi les missions qui lui seront attribuées, le doctorant devra :

· Sélectionner des capteurs existants répondants aux spécifications afin de mettre au point une plateforme de détection 

· Etudier, en conditions de laboratoire, la sélectivité des capteurs vis-à-vis des espèces gazeuses interférentes, à l’aide d’une analyse multivariée

· Définir des algorithmes de prédiction tenant compte de la reproductibilité, de la dérive, de la linéarité et de la variabilité dans des mélanges gazeux complexes et des conditions environnementales variables (température, pression et humidité relative)

· Etudier l'influence du vieillissement des capteurs sur leur réponse et sur les prévisions établies, afin de proposer un algorithme de compensation

·  Enfin, mener des études de cas concrets sur le site de Sainte-Marguerite (Puy-de-Dôme), avec des niveaux d'émissions de CO₂ variables, afin de tester et de valider les plateformes de capteurs développées.

Votre capacité à travailler en mode projet et à faire dialoguer enseignement, recherche et application concrète sera essentielle pour réussir.


🔍 Ce que nous recherchons

Vous êtes titulaire d’un :

· Diplôme Bac + 5 ou équivalent

Et idéalement :

· Titulaire d’un de master 2 dans les domaines suivants : Mesure / Instrumentation / Métrologie ; Acquisition, traitement et analyse de la donnée

· Avec une expérience de stage ou professionnelle dans la recherche (goût prononcé pour la partie expérimentale)

· Junior accepté : oui

Vos atouts supplémentaires :

• La thématique du sujet étant multidisciplinaire de solides connaissances en instrumentations / capteurs, traitements de données, analyse multivariée seront nécessaires. D’autres part, des connaissances en probabilités / statistiques seront également appréciées.

• Le sujet comporte un volet expérimental important mais de solides connaissances numériques seront utiles pour la partie traitement des données (notamment codage sur python)

• Aptitudes pour la communication orale et écrite (notamment en langue anglaise)

🌍 Pourquoi rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne ?

Nous accompagnons chacun de nos collaborateurs sur le chemin de l’excellence, avec la conviction qu’ensemble, nous pouvons avoir un impact durable et significatif sur notre monde.

· Un impact réel : des projets de recherche contractuelle à hauteur de 11 M€/an, majoritairement avec des partenaires industriels, un centre de culture scientifique la Rotonde qui s’engage depuis 25 ans dans la médiation des sciences avec plus de 50 000 visiteurs/an

Alliages métalliques, céramiques, composites… ici, on explore le lien entre procédés, microstructures et propriétés des matériaux.

Grâce à des outils de caractérisation avancée et des modèles multi-échelles, nos enseignants-chercheurs inventent le concept de « Material by design » : concevoir les matériaux dès l’atelier de recherche, pour une performance sur-mesure.

🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vous

En tant que post-doctorant.e, vous êtes au cœur de nos missions en recherche et innovation affectées au centre Science des Matériaux et des Structures (SMS), rattaché au Laboratoire Georges Friedel (unité mixte de recherche CNRS). Alliages métalliques, céramiques, composites… ici, on explore le lien entre procédés, microstructures et propriétés des matériaux.

Grâce à des outils d’élaboration et de caractérisation avancée et des modèles multi-échelles, nous déployons le concept de «Material by design» : concevoir au mieux les matériaux de demain répondant aux enjeux de transition.

Vous aimez la science fondamentale qui change le réel ? C’est ici que ça se passe.

 

Ce post-doctorat s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet VARIMA (VAlorisation des Résidus d’Incinération en Matériaux Avancés) du dispositif Partenariats d'innovation Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes - volet Preuves de Concept. L’incinération des déchets ménagers produit, en plus de l'énergie, des résidus contenant des métaux et des minéraux. Des entreprises récupèrent et recyclent les différents métaux. Cependant, des milliers de tonnes de poussières minérales sont générées et sont généralement envoyées en décharge faute de solution de valorisation.

Ce post-doctorat, d’une durée de 18 mois vise à étudier la valorisation des poussières d’incinération par deux voies d’élaboration : voie géopolymères et voie métallurgie des poudres. Les matériaux obtenus seront ensuite caractérisés au niveau microstructural mais aussi au niveau des propriétés d’usage (propriétés mécanique et thermique ainsi que la tenue à la lixiviation). Le post-doctorant.e contribuera durant la deuxième année de ce CDD à une étude d’impact relative au procédés développés.

🚀 Missions

Ø  Caractérisation physico-chimique et bifurcation des flux de poussières.

  • Mise en œuvre des outils de la plateforme (DRX, FRX, ICP-MS, ATG/DSC, granulométrie laser, etc.

  • Validation et application du protocole de bifurcation technique pour orienter chaque lot vers la voie optimale.

Ø  Développement et optimisation des matrices liantes.

Pilotage des formulations expérimentales en laboratoire pour les deux voies de valorisation afin de lever les verrous scientifiques majeurs (gestion du soufre et des inhibiteurs de prise comme le ZnO).

  • Conception et optimisation des formulations de géopolymères.

  • Optimisation des programmes de frittage des céramiques denses.

Ø  Évaluation de la durabilité, de la conformité réglementaire et lixiviation.

Assurer la qualification technique et environnementale des matériaux développés pour garantir leur transférabilité vers le marché de la construction.

  • Conduire les tests de lixiviation normalisés (NF EN 12457-2) pour démontrer la conformité réglementaire vis-à-vis des seuils de stockage (ISDI) et participer à la rédaction technique de la proposition d’une fiche matière GAMAA et d’un dossier technique d’application.

Assurer le suivi opérationnel quotidien du projet VARIMA et la diffusion des connaissances au sein de l'écosystème concerné.

Sa stratégie 2023-2027 vise à accompagner les transitions écologique, numérique et générationnelle, tout en contribuant à la souveraineté nationale et européenne en microélectronique et numérique.

Le campus Aix-Marseille-Provence, situé à Gardanne, regroupe le Centre Microélectronique de Provence (CMP), des formations d’ingénieurs et de masters, un incubateur technologique et des plateformes de prototypage. Il accueille environ 400 étudiants et 200 personnels de Mines Saint-Étienne et d’entreprises partenaires.

Le CMP dispose d’une salle blanche de 700 m², équipée d’une centaine d’équipements scientifiques répartis en zones de classes 100, 1 000 et 10 000. Cette plateforme est utilisée par les équipes de recherche, les membres académiques et industriels de l’association Micro-PackS, ainsi que pour les formations initiales et continues.

Ses activités couvrent notamment les procédés de couches minces, la photolithographie, la chimie, la caractérisation physique et électrique des matériaux et dispositifs, le micropackaging, l’électronique imprimée et la préparation d’échantillons.

🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vous

Dans le cadre du projet I-novmicro porté par le Campus des Métiers et des Qualifications Industrie du Futur, des modules de formation aux procédés de fabrication en microélectronique sont proposés à des étudiants et apprenants en formation initiale ou continue. La formation se concentrera sur la réalisation de transistor NMOS.

Le Centre de Microélectronique de Provence recrute un ingénieur pour mettre en place et dispenser ces formations, gérer les opérations nécessaires au bon déroulement de celles-ci.

Vos Missions :

Achat d’équipements

La personne retenue gérera, dans un premier temps, l’achat de nouveaux équipements destinés aux formations décrites en introduction.

Mise en place de la formation

La personne sera chargée de développer le module de formation sur le transistor NMOS, en ciblant certains procédés de fabrication. Elle assurera ensuite l’animation des sessions de formation aux procédés microélectroniques associées à ce module.

Ainsi, la personne recrutée devra être former aux procédés standard utilisés en microélectronique (front-end), et effectuer les étapes de fabrication de composants, développées dans le cadre des formations dispensées. Elle sera également en charge du développement de nouveaux procédés. Dans le cadre de ces missions, la ou le titulaire du poste devra utiliser des produits chimiques, et donc en gérer les aspects sécurité. Elle devra utiliser des équipements de caractérisation (ex : microscopie, ellipsométrie, profilométrie) dans le cadre des formations dispensées, et devra pouvoir former des utilisateurs à ces techniques.

Recherche

Etant associé aux départements de recherche du CMP, notamment le département d’électronique flexible, des activités complémentaires de recherche sont envisageables.


🔍 Ce que nous recherchons

Les candidates et candidats doivent être titulaires au minimum d’un bac+5, et avoir une expérience dans la microélectronique, en process et caractérisation en salle blanche.

Une forte polyvalence est requise pour ce poste, avec notamment des compétences en :

  •          Procédés (connaissance et maîtrise) : photolithographie, gravure humide et sèche, dépôts de couches minces et traitements thermiques,

  •          Caractérisation physique de matériaux et dispositifs, et caractérisation électrique de dispositifs.

Une expérience dans le domaine de la formation technique est un réel atout.

Les qualités requises pour le poste sont la pédagogie, l’autonomie, la rigueur, la méthode et l’organisation dans le travail, l’habileté technique et une aisance en communication orale et écrite. La personne retenue devra montrer d’excellentes capacités d’analyse, faire preuve de pragmatisme et d’initiative, avoir l’esprit d’équipe, montrer des qualités relationnelles, et avoir le sens du service.

La pratique de l’anglais est nécessaire, notamment pour la communication avec les équipementiers ou avec certains utilisateurs anglophones de la salle blanche.

🌍 Pourquoi rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne ?

 

Nous accompagnons chacun de nos collaborateurs sur le chemin de l’excellence, avec la conviction qu’ensemble, nous pouvons avoir un impact durable et significatif sur notre monde.

Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c’est l’opportunité de trouver :

·         Un environnement stimulant : des moyens expérimentaux de pointe, un réseau international solide (T.I.M.E., EULIST) et des campus à taille humaine avec un environnement urbain

·         Un impact réel : des projets de recherche contractuelle à hauteur de 11 M€/an, majoritairement avec des partenaires industriels, un centre de culture scientifique la Rotonde qui s’engage depuis 25 ans dans la médiation des sciences avec plus de 50 000 visiteurs/an

·         Une qualité de vie incomparable : 49 jours de congés et RTT, télétravail partiel, prise en charge des transports en commun à 75 %, soutien financier au covoiturage et au vélo et un baromètre social où 83 % des collaborateurs plébiscitent la qualité de vie au travail

Construisons un avenir plus durable, à travers la science, l’ingénierie, et des projets qui font sens.

title: Enterprise Customer Success Manager
description:
UpSlide is the document production layer for financial services. We orchestrate LLMs, machine learning, and workflow agents within Microsoft 365 to deliver reliable, quality outputs in the most efficient and cost-effective way.

As a Microsoft Solutions Partner, with 14+ years supporting financial services teams, we bring together expertise from the tech, finance and design fields to help clients like KPMG, BNP Paribas, Rothschild & Co. boost productivity while improving brand consistency across their corporate documents. 

We are a certified B Corporation, upholding the belief that businesses should have a positive impact on society.

✨ Our values

Our values guide our approach to work and are at the heart of our recruitment process. To join our team, we look for individuals who value:

  • Excellence: We think that every detail counts, and we place great importance on the quality of our deliverables.

  • Trust: We are passionate, committed, and free to act with autonomy.

  • Happiness at work: We enjoy looking on the bright side and we share our enthusiasm with our colleagues and clients.

🤝 The team

You will join our Enterprise Customer Success team for the EMEA, APAC, and NA regions, a group of Customer Success Managers, each responsible for a focused portfolio of our largest and most strategic accounts.

You will join a team of 6, including 5 CSMs and Majhon, Head of Customer Success Enterprise, who will support you in achieving your goals. You will also be part of a global Customer Success community across our five offices.

Here is what the Go-To-Market organization looks like at UpSlide:

  • Account Executives: Prospect, acquire new business acquisition and expand existing accounts

  • Consultants: Lead implementation projects, deliver client training, and ensure successful deployment

  • Customer Success Managers: Own a portfolio of accounts end-to-end, driving retention, renewal signing, expansion within existing entities, value realization, and long-term account growth

  • Support Engineers: Resolve day-to-day technical questions and issues, and ensure a smooth customer experience

🖋️ Your responsibilities

As an Enterprise Customer Success Manager, you will own the end-to-end relationship with a portfolio of our largest, most strategic accounts. You will build deep, multi-threaded relationships with key stakeholders, lead high-impact business reviews, and act as a trusted advisor, proactively protecting and growing revenue across your book through both retention and expansion.

This is a role for someone who thrives on depth: fewer accounts, higher stakes, and the ability to build genuine, senior-level relationships that compound into long-term growth, while knowing how to sync with regional counterparts on accounts that span multiple geographies, keeping a global view of the relationship without owning every part of it directly.

Account Ownership & Revenue Growth (50%)

Own the business performance, strategy, and health of your portfolio of strategic accounts:

  • Take full ownership of your portfolio (ARR, NRR, renewal, risk level)

  • Build and execute structured, tailored account plans for 100% of your accounts, with clear growth and retention objectives

  • Proactively identify both expansion opportunities and churn risk through data analysis and direct relationship insight, and own them through to resolution or close

  • Monitor account health through usage data, adoption metrics, contact network and mapping, and stakeholder engagement

  • Maintain accurate forecasting (renewals, churn, upsell potential) and rigorous CRM discipline (Salesforce accuracy and completeness)

Customer Value & Expertise (40%)

Drive measurable value and position UpSlide as a strategic partner:

  • Lead high-impact Business Reviews focused on ROI and value realization

  • Lead complex or sensitive conversations (renegotiation, escalations, dissatisfaction) with confidence and clarity

  • Secure executive sponsors and build multi-threaded relationships within each account

  • Develop and maintain strong product expertise and a deep understanding of client industries and use cases

  • Craft value-driven narratives tailored to each stakeholder's priorities

Cross-functional Collaboration (10%)

Align with internal teams to maximize customer outcomes and business impact:

  • Partner with Sales on the account expansion strategy and account mapping

  • Collaborate with Professional Services when deeper deployment or training support is needed

  • Work closely with Product and Support to relay structured feedback and improve the customer experience

  • Coordinate with CSMs in other regions on shared or global accounts

  • Contribute to Customer Success best practices and performance improvement initiatives

To work on these tasks, you will mainly use the following tools: Microsoft Office, UpSlide, Salesforce, Gong, PowerBI, and Notion (or local equivalents).

⚡Your goals

You will be assessed on:

  • Net Revenue Retention (NRR)

  • Churn

  • Expansion / upsell contribution

  • Depth and health of executive relationships across your portfolio

  • Ability to maintain full ownership and visibility on shared accounts


You are a great fit if you have:

  • 3+ years of experience in Customer Success, Account Management, or a related client-facing/revenue role, including managing enterprise or large, multi-entity accounts in a B2B environment

  • Proven experience managing renewals and churn on strategic / enterprise accounts, with meaningful revenue responsibility

  • A proven track record of generating expansion (upsell/cross-sell) within an enterprise account base

  • Experience in autonomously managing a portfolio of large or multi-entity accounts with significant revenue responsibility

  • Confidence leading executive-level conversations, including complex or difficult ones (renegotiation, dissatisfaction, escalations)

  • Advanced negotiation skills

  • A structured, strategic approach to account planning (objectives, stakeholders, action plans)

  • A value- and ROI-oriented mindset, able to build and defend a business case with senior stakeholders

  • Operational rigor: accurate CRM data, reliable follow-up, dependable forecasting

  • Excellent written and verbal communication in English and French

  • Comfortable working in an international environment, engaging with senior and executive stakeholders

We’d love it if you have:

  • Experience with a CRM / Customer Success platform (Salesforce, Planhat, or equivalent) and analytics / BI tools (PowerBI or equivalent)

  • Knowledge of the financial services/consulting sector

  • Experience managing group or multi-entity account structures

  • Familiarity with SaaS metrics (ARR, NRR, churn, forecasting) and reporting to leadership

  • Fluency in another language (e.g. German)

✨ If you don’t tick all the boxes but you think you’d be a great fit, please apply and tell us why.

Recruitment process

  1. Screening call with Talent Acquisition: A conversation to walk through your experience, motivation, and fit for the role.

  2. Interview with your future manager and a team-meet: A deeper dive into your Customer Success experience and approach to account management. This also includes a live exercise reflecting real challenges of the role, followed by a conversation with members of the wider team.

  3. Final conversation with leadership: A closing discussion to align on ambition, expectations, and next steps.

🚀 We'll conduct a reference check to learn how to help you thrive. On average, our process lasts 3 weeks.

What we offer

🌍 International environment: Start-up with five offices (Paris, London, Berlin, New York, Singapore) and users in more than 60 countries

About Us

Point One Navigation is building the future of precise location. Our mission is to deliver a unified location platform that enables autonomy, safety, and efficiency across industries from robotics to transportation. Role Outcome

The Network Customer Support Engineer owns the customer support experience tied to the reliability, visibility, and operational health of Point One’s correction network.

This is a player-coach role. You will personally handle complex technical support cases while also leading the operational systems, monitoring, and processes that ensure the network performs reliably at scale.

Success in this role means:

  • Potential customer facing issues are identified and addressed before they impact customers.

  • When incidents do occur, they are resolved quickly with clear communication and strong root-cause analysis.

  • The organization has clear visibility into network health, operational trends, and customer friction.

  • A scalable network operations and support function is built as the company and network footprint grow.

Immediate Areas of Focus

Own the customer experience of our Network

  • Work with our Network Operations team to understand incidents that affect the customer experience

  • Identify emerging issues and collaborate with engineering and manufacturing teams to understand and support the resolution of those issues.

  • Understand available metrics and dashboards and contribute to the development of these tools to allow for the targeted resolution of customer questions.

Deliver High-Quality Technical Support

  • Liaison between Engineering, Network Operations and FAE and FDE team to support the customer.

  • Personally manage high-impact or technically complex support cases.

  • Partner closely with FAEs, Product, and Engineering to diagnose issues and close the loop with customers.

  • Ensure customers receive clear, confident communication during investigations and incidents.

  • Model best-in-class technical troubleshooting and customer engagement practices for the team.

Build the Foundation for a Scalable Operations & Support Function

  • Design and implement systems that enable both network operations and customer support to scale.

  • Define a support ticket taxonomy that reflects customer use cases, technical complexity, and operational impact.

  • Support Network Ops team on operational metrics such as:

    • Network uptime and availability

    • Incident response and resolution times

    • Support response and resolution times

    • Alert quality and monitoring coverage

    • Document operational procedures, escalation paths, and ownership models.

  • Develop automation and tooling to reduce manual work and improve operational efficiency.

Surface Operational and Customer Insights

  • Identify patterns across support tickets, network events, and operational data.

  • Translate operational signals into actionable insights for Product and Engineering.

  • Ensure recurring issues and infrastructure gaps are clearly surfaced and prioritized.

  • Create lightweight reporting that gives leadership visibility into network reliability, operational trends, and customer friction.

Establish Visibility Into Customer Experience

  • Define and implement the right metrics for understanding customer experience and operational impact.

  • Establish mechanisms to collect structured customer feedback without creating noise.

  • Use both operational data and customer feedback to drive continuous improvement.

Coach and Develop the Operations & Support Function

  • Act as a player-coach, leading through hands-on operational work while building the foundations of the team.

  • Train and mentor support engineers on troubleshooting methodology, operational awareness, and customer communication.

  • Establish clear expectations for technical depth, ownership, and responsiveness.

  • Continuously raise the operational and support bar as the team grows.

Qualifications

  • Fluency in a two European languages in addition to English.

  • Experience in a player-coach technical operations or support role where you owned both hands-on troubleshooting and operational systems.

  • Strong technical background in GPS/GNSS, precise localization, geospatial infrastructure, or closely related domains (robotics, autonomy, embedded systems, positioning technologies).

  • Experience operating or supporting distributed infrastructure or network-based systems.

  • Demonstrated ability to build or significantly improve monitoring, alerting, and operational processes.

  • Proven experience troubleshooting complex technical systems and working directly with customers.

  • Experience conducting incident response and root cause analysis.

  • Ability to define metrics, processes, and documentation without over-engineering.

  • Comfort working cross-functionally with Engineering, Product, and Go-To-Market teams in a fast-moving environment.

  • Bias toward ownership, operational excellence, and continuous improvement.

Our Cultural Foundation

At Point One, our cultural and operating design is built around one guiding principle: we must move with extreme speed and efficiency of effort to stay in a leadership position.

This environment gives people a high level of autonomy and the ability to make a real impact. It also challenges every team member to grow — both professionally and personally. Because we focus on promoting from within rather than relying on external hiring, the opportunities for advancement are tremendous for those who seek them.

That said, growth only comes from delivering in the present. What matters most is the job to be done today, not the job you want tomorrow. When we all focus on today’s outcomes with excellence, the path to greater responsibility and growth naturally follows.

We think about our culture in two dimensions:

How We Show Up Every Day

These are the behaviors we expect every team member to bring to work — the foundation of being a consummate, high-output teammate:

  • Trust / Assume Best Intent — Trust allows us to move fast. When we start from trust, we spend no time second-guessing or looking for ulterior motives and thus focus all our energy on acting.

  • High Output, Action Oriented — Our default posture is “yes.” We bias toward action and deliver results quickly, knowing that speed and efficiency compound into impact as we unblock others around us.

  • Divine Discontent — We’re never satisfied with the status quo and are self-motivated to improve ourselves, our work, and our company. We actively seek feedback in real-time to shorten improvement cycles.

  • No Ego, One Team — Collaboration without ego creates leverage. When we win as one team, we eliminate friction and move faster together.

  • Self Accountability — Taking ownership is the straightest line to learning, self-improvement, and correcting our course of action. And blaming others around us is a fast path to destroying trust.

Operating Principles

These are the systems and norms that amplify speed and efficiency at the company level:

  • Edge Innovation — We bias toward action over approval. Experiment, decide, and move — failure is just a step toward faster learning.

  • No Hierarchies — We practice self-prioritization and go direct to the source. Flattening layers reduces drag and maximizes autonomy.

  • Customer Experience First — We optimize for the end-to-end customer outcome, not functional or departmental efficiency. This focus cuts waste, aligns priorities, and ensures we spend effort where it matters most.

title: (Senior) Integration Engineer, ERP (Oracle)
description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains.

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times.

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies.

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America.

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.

About the role

BLP only works when it talks to our customers’ ERP systems. As an Integration Engineer, you build and own those connections and keep live integrations running for enterprise customers. Every new ERP system is a new problem to solve. You’ll lead our Oracle integrations across Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite and JD Edwards, while also contributing to other integrations.

 

What you’ll do

  • Own our integrations with Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite and JD Edwards and ensure their market fit, usability and reliability.

  • Design and implement interfaces for diverse protocols: REST, SOAP, direct DB access and file transfers.

  • Explore new ERP systems and determine the best way to connect them.

  • Build new ERP integrations, often in close collaboration with pilot customers.

  • Own existing integrations end to end, including issue resolution, and document them so teammates can pick them up.

  • Enable technical project managers to consult on, install and configure mature integrations.

 

What you'll bring

  • Hands-on integration experience with Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite or JD Edwards EnterpriseOne, ideally more than one. You have built or maintained interfaces yourself, not only used the system as a functional consultant or key user.

  • Experience with the native interfaces of at least one of these:

    • Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP: REST and SOAP web services, File-Based Data Import (FBDI) through the ERP Integration Service, and data extraction with BI Publisher or BI Cloud Connector (BICC).

    • NetSuite: SuiteTalk REST and SOAP web services, SuiteQL, SuiteScript 2.x (e.g., RESTlets, Map/Reduce scripts), and Token-Based Authentication or OAuth 2.0.

    • JD Edwards EnterpriseOne: AIS Server and Orchestrator, Business Services (BSSV), and Z-file interface tables (e.g., F0411Z1) with their batch processors.

  • A good understanding of purchase-to-pay data in Oracle ERPs: suppliers, purchase orders, receipts and supplier invoice matching.

  • Solid programming skills in at least one backend language. We build our integrations in Go. If you come from Java, C#, Python or similar and are keen to pick up Go, that works for us.

  • A degree in computer science or a related field, or equivalent experience.

  • A structured, self-reliant way of working, and ideally experience in a client-facing role.

  • Fluent English. German is a plus, as most of our customers are in the DACH region.

Nice to have:

  • Experience with both cloud (Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite) and on-premise (JD Edwards) environments, and the constraints of each (e.g., no direct database access in Fusion, governance limits in NetSuite).

  • Extensive experience with SQL, common data formats (JSON, XML, CSV) and transports (REST/SOAP APIs, SFTP).

  • Familiarity with modern engineering practices: Git, code reviews, automated testing and CI/CD.

  • Integration experience with other ERPs, such as SAP, Microsoft Dynamics or Infor.

 

Integration Engineer or Senior Integration Engineer

We hire at both levels. Four things decide where you start: years of experience, breadth of experience, coaching experience and scope.

Integration Engineer

  • Years: 2+ years of hands-on integration work, including Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite or JD Edwards.

  • Breadth: in-depth experience with one Oracle ERP and its interfaces.

  • Coaching: you learn quickly from senior colleagues and share what you learn with the team.

  • Scope: you deliver and maintain integrations and resolve issues independently, with guidance on architecture decisions.

Senior Integration Engineer

  • Years: 5+ years of hands-on integration work, several of them with Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite or JD Edwards.

  • Breadth: integration experience across two or more of Fusion, NetSuite and JD Edwards, or across Oracle and other ERPs, in cloud and on-premise environments.

  • Coaching: you have coached or mentored other engineers and help technical project managers grow.

  • Scope: you own our Oracle integrations end to end, set technical direction and take on the most complex customer cases.

Why BLP

  • Real impact: your integrations decide whether a customer goes live.

  • Breadth: Oracle, Infor, Microsoft Dynamics and many other ERPs, plus EDI and e-invoicing standards.

  • Growth: fast-tracked growth, with promotions and a bonus scheme that includes company shares.

  • Team: regular team events.

Practical information

  • Location: our Zurich office, hybrid with 3+ office days per week, or remotely from anywhere in Europe.

  • If you work remotely, we pay for regular visits and stays in Zurich.

  • Employment: full-time, permanent.

 

Learn more about blp and our values at blp.digital/company/careers.

title: Head of Finance & Administration
description:
The role

H55 is looking for a versatile and hands on Head of Finance & Administration to lead its corporate functions and ensure the effective running of its Swiss site.

This broad leadership role combines a solid finance background with strong corporate governance and practical operational management. Working closely with the CEO and leadership team, you will connect people, priorities and resources, providing the structure and support needed to deliver the company’s business objectives.

You will develop a thorough understanding of H55’s corporate framework, including its shareholder arrangements, financing agreements and key contractual commitments, and translate these obligations into clear responsibilities, practical policies and timely action.

You will oversee finance, HR, IT, facilities and general administration, supported by internal specialists and external partners. As a central point of coordination for Swiss site matters, you will help teams resolve operational issues, improve ways of working and ensure corporate services meet the needs of the business.

Key responsibilities

Corporate governance and administration

  • Coordinate Board and shareholder matters with the CEO and legal counsel, including meeting preparation, resolutions, corporate records and follow through on decisions.

  • Maintain a clear overview of the company’s corporate structure, shareholder arrangements, financing agreements and material contractual commitments.

  • Track related obligations and deadlines, ensuring clear ownership and timely action across relevant functions.

  • Ensure governance requirements, delegated authorities and approval processes are understood and applied.

  • Manage relationships with external legal advisers, insurers and corporate service providers.

Policies, compliance and internal controls

  • Coordinate the development, implementation and review of company policies in line with business needs, investor commitments and applicable requirements.

  • Work with functional owners on anti corruption, cybersecurity and incident response, related party transactions, internal financial controls, global trade controls, personal data protection, and health and safety.

  • Translate policies into practical procedures, with clear responsibilities and guidance for employees and managers.

  • Coordinate communication and training, maintaining appropriate records.

  • Monitor implementation, address gaps with relevant owners and bring matters requiring attention to the leadership team.

Swiss site and corporate services

  • Coordinate Swiss site administration and corporate support activities, working closely with production, engineering and other teams.

  • Oversee facilities, workplace services and external providers, ensuring a safe and effective working environment.

  • Help resolve site issues and coordinate improvements that support daily operations.

  • Oversee IT services and infrastructure through internal resources and external partners.

  • Drive improvements in digital tools, systems and administrative processes.

  • Coordinate site procedures and business continuity arrangements with relevant specialists.

HR oversight and organisational support

  • Oversee the HR function, supporting the HR team in delivering effective people processes and reliable daily operations.

  • Work with the CEO and managers on workforce planning, organisational changes and recruitment priorities.

  • Ensure employment administration, payroll coordination and HR policies are managed consistently and appropriately.

  • Support clear internal communication and effective collaboration across teams.

Financial management and business support

  • Oversee budgeting, forecasting, cash flow planning and financial reporting, supported by internal finance resources and external partners.

  • Ensure reliable accounting, statutory reporting, tax and audit processes.

  • Provide clear financial visibility to support business decisions and resource allocation.

  • Maintain appropriate financial controls, spending discipline and approval processes.

  • Monitor costs and commitments with budget owners and programme teams.

  • Support investor reporting, financing activities and due diligence when required.

Leadership and continuous improvement

  • Lead and support a small multidisciplinary team, coordinating external expertise where needed.

  • Set priorities, allocate resources and ensure actions are completed.

  • Build trusted working relationships with managers and colleagues across the organisation.

  • Simplify processes and adapt corporate services as the business evolves.

Your profile

  • Experience in a broad finance and administration, corporate services or business operations leadership role.

  • A solid finance background, with experience taking responsibility beyond the finance function.

  • Strong understanding of corporate governance and confidence working with corporate documents, contractual commitments and legal advisers.

  • Experience implementing policies and translating compliance requirements into practical ways of working.

  • Experience coordinating site operations or corporate support functions, ideally in a technology or industrial environment.

  • Familiarity with the Swiss business environment and relevant administrative and statutory requirements.

  • Ability to lead across different functions, drawing on the expertise of colleagues and external partners.

  • Sound judgement, discretion and the ability to build trust with people across the organisation.

  • A practical, collaborative approach, with strong organisational skills and a willingness to get involved in day to day matters.

  • Fluent English and French.

  • A relevant qualification in finance, business administration or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

You do not need to be a specialist in every function. You should be comfortable asking the right questions, bringing together the right expertise and taking responsibility for progress.

Why join H55?

At H55, you will work closely with the people developing electric aviation technology and help create the conditions for them to succeed. Your decisions will shape how we work, support our teams and move the business forward.

You will have room to bring ideas, improve how things are done and see the results of your work. If you enjoy connecting people, making sense of complex issues and turning decisions into action, this role offers the opportunity to do all three.

title: Site Reliability Engineer
description:
About Us:

DeepJudge is Switzerland’s leading AI and ICT scale-up, transforming how law firms and legal departments access and leverage their knowledge. Founded by former Google search engineers with PhDs in AI from ETH Zurich, and backed by top-tier Silicon Valley investors, we are building the intelligence layer that powers the legal industry.

Every firm can license the same AI models, but no two firms share the same institutional knowledge. Decades of experience, work product, and precedent are often trapped across systems, underused and inaccessible. DeepJudge makes this expertise instantly available through world-class enterprise search and AI infrastructure, enabling firms to automate workflows, build knowledge-powered applications, and turn experience into a lasting advantage.

Our technology is trusted by many of the world’s leading law firms, including Freshfields, Gunderson Dettmer, Holland & Knight, Arent Fox, and Cozen O’Connor. Headquartered in Switzerland with a growing team across North America, we are expanding rapidly and shaping the future of how professional knowledge is discovered and applied.

At DeepJudge, we move fast, think rigorously, and care deeply about what we build. We combine cutting-edge research with close collaboration with our clients to deliver solutions that truly make an impact. If you want to be part of a team defining how AI transforms high-stakes knowledge work, this is the place to do it.


About the role:

As a Site Reliability Engineer at DeepJudge, you own the reliability of the systems that leading law firms depend on every day. We run our AI search platform in dedicated production environments, each a large-scale search and retrieval system operating at very high data volumes, alongside our ingestion pipelines and data stores, on container-orchestrated infrastructure across multiple public and private clouds. Keeping those environments fast, available, and trustworthy is a genuine engineering challenge, and it's your mission.

This is a technical, infrastructure-focused role: you'll spend your time in systems, code, and telemetry. You'll harden the platform so that classes of failure can't recur, build observability and SLOs to let us see problems before they surface, plan capacity ahead of relentless data growth, and automate away the toil of safely operating many production environments. You'll work across our deployment and infrastructure-as-code and partner closely with product engineering to feed reliability learnings back into the platform. If you like operating serious distributed systems at scale and turning firefighting into engineered reliability, this role is for you.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Owning the availability, latency and performance of our production environments: large-scale search and retrieval services, ingestion and data stores on container-orchestrated infrastructure across multiple public and private clouds

  • Owning the cloud infrastructure across multiple public and private clouds, networking, identity and access, compute and storage, and managing cloud capacity, quotas and cost as the fleet grows

  • Improving deployment and infrastructure through code: GitOps-based configuration and deployment and infrastructure-as-code across our public and private clouds, with safe, previewed, recoverable production changes

  • Defining and instrumenting SLOs and error budgets and building the dashboards, metrics and alerting that make production observable and actionable

  • Reducing operational toil through automation and internal tooling written in Python and / or Go

  • Provisioning and standardizing new production environments to a defined reliability bar

You're a great fit if you:

  • Have 3+ years in SRE, production / platform engineering, or infrastructure-heavy software engineering, operating real production systems under reliability expectations

  • Are strong at container-orchestration operations in production and comfortable on at least one major public cloud

  • Have solid cloud infrastructure experience on a major public cloud and a working grasp of cloud capacity, quotas, and cost

  • Practice observability hands-on with metrics, logs and traces, and use it to root-cause live incidents

  • Work fluently with infrastructure-as-code and GitOps

  • Can code in Python and / or Go for automation, tooling, and reading and patching service code.

  • Bring sound production judgment and document your work clearly for other engineers

  • Bonus: experience operating a large-scale search or distributed data system, database operations, dedicated / enterprise-deployed software, or AI / enterprise-search infrastructure in regulated domains

What you can look forward to:

  • Owning the reliability of systems that the world's leading law firms rely on: real scale, real impact

  • Deep, hands-on work with modern infrastructure: distributed search at very large scale, container orchestration across multiple clouds, and a mature infrastructure-as-code and GitOps stack

  • A rigorous, high-urgency engineering culture founded by ex-Google search engineers and ETH Zurich AI PhDs

  • The chance to build the reliability discipline, SLOs, incident practice, automation, from a strong foundation, not inherit a rigid one

  • A collaborative team in Zurich shaping how AI transforms professional knowledge work

At DeepJudge, we believe great teams are built on diverse perspectives and experiences. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to fostering an inclusive, high-performance culture where everyone can thrive. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

It is also most of what a protein costs to make, which makes procurement one of the biggest levers on gross margin in the business.

So far scientists have bought what they need, decisions get made in hours, and nothing blocks an experiment. That was the right trade while we were proving the thing works. But we are multiplying lab throughput several times over, and at that volume procurement becomes a discipline: real terms with the suppliers we already buy from heavily, qualified second sources where we currently have one, inventory that is planned rather than remembered. Nobody has taken that on yet.

You would be our first dedicated supply chain hire, and it is hands-on — you do the sourcing and the negotiating yourself. What You'll Do

  • Negotiate. Build the supplier relationships across our DNA, reagent, biosensor and catalog-protein vendors, put volume commitments and pricing agreements in place, and go get the margin back.

  • Drive down the cost of a protein. Go category by category and take cost out of each. A few francs per protein, multiplied across the volumes we are heading toward, is a seven-figure line.

  • Stay ahead of the science. When R&D says they are adding a new assay next quarter, you should already be sourcing the reagents for it.

  • Set inventory policy, and make the numbers true. Reorder points and safety stock, so we never stall a customer experiment on a stockout and never have six figures of reagents quietly expiring in a freezer. You decide what should be on the shelves and how much of it.

  • You think in margins. Saving a few francs per protein across tens of thousands of proteins a month is a number that should make you sit up.

  • You automate. We run on Claude Code across the company and our lab system has an API. The best version of this person is writing scripts against our systems and our vendors' systems, not clicking through them. If your instinct is that procurement is a portal-and-email job, we will frustrate each other.

  • Obsessive about the details that bite. Lead times, expiry dates, lot numbers, minimum order quantities. Nothing falls through.

Scope

DataSnipper builds the AI that auditors and finance teams rely on to do that work with confidence: agents designed around how audits are actually performed, a platform firms trust with their most sensitive client evidence, and a team built around former auditors who know the work firsthand. We want to define how the profession works in the age of AI.

More than 600,000 professionals across 175 countries use DataSnipper, including all Big Four firms, Fortune 500 companies, and government agencies. In 2025 alone, we delivered over $1.4 billion in productivity savings for our customers. Backed by Index Ventures and Insight Partners, we are one of the fastest-growing companies in AI for audit, and the fastest-growing tech company in the Netherlands two years running.

Everything we build starts from one principle: AI in audit has to be something professionals can trust, verify, and defend. Joining now means helping lead the profession's shift from manual testing to agentic execution.


The Role


Partnerships are one of DataSnipper's most important growth levers. Across every major market, the consulting firms, technology platforms, and professional networks that organizations rely on shape which technologies their teams and clients adopt. As AI changes how audit work gets done, those partners are deciding who to build with.

As Strategic Partnerships Lead, you will lead, build, and launch DataSnipper's partnerships across Europe and the wider EMEA region, spanning our consulting alliances, key technology partners, and strategic relationships across the audit ecosystem and beyond. Our European ecosystem already includes relationships with leading consulting firms and regional networks. Your job is to scale it, and to build what comes next: new partner programs, new markets, and new commercial models.

This is an entrepreneurial, quota-carrying role with a broad remit and room to build. You will report to the Global Partnerships Leader and work closely with our EMEA Sales, Customer Success, Product, and Marketing teams.


What You Will Work On

  • Own and grow a portfolio of strategic partners across Europe, including consulting firms, technology platforms, and regional networks, and act as their senior counterpart at DataSnipper.

  • Source, assess, and close new partnerships, from referral and co-sell arrangements to resell models, prioritized against DataSnipper's growth goals.

  • Work with consulting partners to help them advise their clients on bringing AI into audit and finance, with DataSnipper at the center of that work.

  • Create the enablement, playbooks, and co-marketing assets partners need to position and deliver DataSnipper with confidence.

  • Be a visible face of DataSnipper across the region, at partner summits, field events, and industry forums.

  • Willingness to embrace global business and travel.

What You Bring

  • 5 to 7 years of experience in partnerships, business development, or a senior commercial role, ideally in B2B SaaS, AI, or financial technology.

  • A proven track record of independently managing and growing complex, multi-stakeholder partnerships from identification through to revenue impact.

  • Strong commercial acumen, with the ability to negotiate partnership structures, co-sell agreements, and commercial terms with senior counterparts.

  • Experience building joint go-to-market programs and driving pipeline through partner channels across more than one European market.

  • Excellent relationship-building and influencing skills, with the credibility to work as a peer with firm leadership, from alliance leads to managing directors and partners.

  • Existing relationships with consulting firm leadership in Europe are a strong advantage.

How You Work

  • Entrepreneurial. When you spot a gap, you build what fills it, playbook or not.

  • Close to the work. You dig into how audit gets done, how firms make decisions, and where AI changes the economics.

Why This Role, Why Now

A $100M Series B led by Index Ventures at a $1B valuation, building on earlier investment from Insight Partners. Ranked #1 on the Deloitte Technology Fast 50 in 2023 and 2024, named to the Forbes Fintech 50 for 2026, and one of the fastest-growing companies in AI for audit.

title: Engineering Manager, Billing & Monetization
description:
About the role

Every customer's path through DataSnipper, from first sign-up to first agent run to renewal, runs on systems your team owns. We are hiring an Engineering Manager in our Amsterdam office to lead Billing & Monetization: how customers get in, what they are entitled to, and how AI usage turns into revenue.

Why DataSnipper?

The hardest AI problems aren't about getting an answer fast. They're about getting one people can trust.

We believe trust is essential to how society works. Every day, we rely on information that's been independently verified, from financial statements to the products we buy, to the sustainability claims companies make. Behind that trust are audit and finance professionals who examine evidence, verify information and hold organizations accountable.

At DataSnipper, we build AI solutions that empowers those professionals. By making evidence easier to trace and verify, we help them focus on the judgment and expertise that make their work so important.


For our product and engineering team, this is where things get exciting. In audit, a plausible answer isn't good enough. Every output must be explainable and traceable back to its source. We've just launched a brand-new agentic platform, Alwin by DataSnipper. AI agents running in the cloud across hundreds of documents at once, reasoning across PDF, Word and Excel, with a full audit trail behind every step. There are lots of greenfield problems ahead, and real room to shape what we build and how we build it.

And we build at scale. More than 600,000 professionals across 3,000+ organizations in 175 countries rely on DataSnipper, including Fortune 500 companies, government agencies and all Big Four audit firms. In 2025 alone, the DataSnipper platform delivered more than $1.4 billion in productivity savings to is customers. Backed by a $100 million Series B led by Index Ventures, at a $1 billion valuation, and as proud members of 1% for the Planet, we care about how we grow, not just how fast.

If you want to build AI that professionals trust with work that really matters, this is your chance to help shape the future of audit and finance and do the best work of your career along the way.

title: Senior Product Manager Transport (Equipment)
description:
About us

Rentman is a B2B SaaS scale-up building a smart, powerful operations management platform to support event and media production teams. Our users plan everything from small shoots to massive festivals in 70+ countries, and they all rely on Rentman to keep their gear, people, and timing perfectly in sync. We’re based in Utrecht (NL) with a second office in Toronto (CA), and our 100+ team members work in a culture that’s open, flat, and inclusive, where curiosity drives us, ownership matters, and everyone has the freedom to challenge ideas and make an impact. Check out our public roadmap to see what’s coming next!

Mission of this role

Getting equipment to and from an event, on time and in one piece, is one of the most critical things our customers do, and one of the hardest. Heavy, specialised, often fragile gear. Fixed vehicle and crew capacity. Round trips rather than one-way drops. Our customers solve this every week, mostly with spreadsheets, phone calls and hard-won instinct.

Transport is a priority on our roadmap, and we're bringing in dedicated ownership to make sure we deliver on it: how customers plan loads, sequence stops and optimise routes across their fleet. This role owns that outcome from the ground up. You'll start by getting close to customers to find the first slice of the problem they'll genuinely want to have solved, ship it, and build the roadmap from there.

Which features ship is yours to decide. You'll be shaping the domain and its roadmap, with the freedom to define how the product takes form. That's a rare amount of ownership for a PM, building something new from first principles, with real trust in how you get there.

What you'll do

  • Own Transport end to end: Running the full release train for your value stream: discovery, scoping, design, development, launch and post-launch tracking.

  • Run customer discovery yourself, in the field: Talk to rental companies about how they plan, staff and execute transport today: warehouse-to-venue routing, multi-stop and multi-vehicle loads, load order, crew and vehicle capacity, and the constraints that make equipment transport harder than generic delivery routing.

  • Define the first sellable increment. Find the smallest thing customers will genuinely pay for, ship it, and be able to explain why that slice was the right first bet.

  • Build and own a sequenced, evidence-based roadmap with the Head of Product, aligned to company goals and product strategy. And explain the prioritisation to sales, support and management so they can plan against it.

  • Translate routing and logistics complexity into buildable scope: multi-stop optimisation, time windows, vehicle and crew capacity, mapping and routing APIs, and the build-vs-buy decisions that come with them.

  • Define success before you build it: Every feature carries a business goal, product briefs stay current, a live dashboard goes up at launch, and you drive go-to-market together with Product Marketing, Support, Sales and Content & Community.

What we are looking for

  • 5+ years as a Product Manager in B2B SaaS.

  • You've owned a product area end to end. From discovery through launch and post-launch tracking, not a backlog-only PO role.

  • You're comfortable with operationally complex problems: routing, scheduling, fleet or capacity planning, supply chain, field service. A logistics background is a plus, not a must.

  • You work from data. You can show how you set a success metric, what you did when it was missed, and how you make the business case behind a product call.

  • You've run customer discovery yourself, not through a research team, and you can make and defend scope calls on partial evidence.

Nice to haves

  • Product experience in route optimisation, fleet management, field service or supply chain / TMS, or hands-on experience with mapping and routing APIs and platforms (Google Maps Platform, HERE, Mapbox, route-optimisation engines).

  • Experience building a product domain or team from scratch (0-to-1), not only taking one over.

  • Experience in the live event, AV or equipment rental industry, and/or Dutch, German or French.

What you’ll get

  • Competitive salary based on experience, plus 8% holiday allowance

  • A results-based bonus based on company performance (up to a full 13th month's salary)

  • 25 vacation days to recharge

  • Earn an extra day of PTO for each year at Rentman, from your second anniversary up to five years.

  • A 4-week paid sabbatical after 5 years to go on an adventure

  • Flexible WFH policy & work from anywhere for 4 weeks a year

  • Pension plan through BrightPensioen

title: Network Engineer
description:
About the role

Help build the networks connecting SkyNRG’s offices and future production sites!

As we scale Sustainable Aviation Fuel production, secure and reliable connectivity between our IT and operational environments becomes increasingly critical. We are looking for a Network Engineer (IT/OT) to design, build, and operate the network architecture supporting our Amsterdam headquarters, first production facility, and future sites.

This is a hands-on role with real influence over how our network landscape develops, from routing, switching and Wi-Fi to firewalls, IT/OT segmentation, and secure remote access.

Reporting to the IT Operations & Infrastructure Manager, the role works closely with IT, security, plant engineering, and automation partners.

Your Responsibilities:

  • Design, build, and operate IT and OT network infrastructure at headquarters and production sites, from Purdue Level 3 upward and at the boundary with plant control systems

  • Manage and optimize our Fortinet (IT) and Palo Alto (OT) firewall environments, including rule sets, segmentation, and the industrial DMZ

  • Operate Cisco Catalyst switching and Meraki wireless at our production sites, alongside the office network at headquarters

  • Implement and maintain secure remote access for employees and vendors, including zero trust access

  • Deploy and operate Nozomi Networks for OT asset visibility and threat detection, and integrate network and OT logs into our SIEM (Microsoft Sentinel)

  • Support incident response together with our security team and managed SOC provider, and contribute to NIS2 compliance activities

This is an opportunity to build an IT/OT network from the ground up rather than maintain a legacy landscape. You will work with a modern technology stack, have real influence over architecture decisions, and see the direct impact of your work on our operational reliability and cybersecurity maturity.

The position is based at our headquarters in Amsterdam. Expect regular travel to the production site during construction and commissioning, becoming occasional once the site is in operation.

Your profile

As a growing company in a rapidly evolving industry, we are looking for people who embrace change and are motivated to actively contribute to building and scaling our business. You are someone who feels comfortable in an entrepreneurial environment, takes ownership, and thrives when things are still developing.

You recognize yourself in the following:

  • 5+ years of experience as a Network Engineer, including hands-on responsibility for enterprise firewall environments

  • Strong experience with Fortinet FortiGate or Palo Alto Networks firewalls, and the willingness to master the other

  • Solid knowledge of routing, switching (preferably Cisco Catalyst), wireless, VPN technologies, and network security best practices

  • Experience with, or strong knowledge of, OT and industrial network environments, including ICS and SCADA systems

  • Understanding of IT/OT segmentation principles and frameworks such as IEC 62443 and the Purdue Model, including industrial DMZ design

  • Experience with OT monitoring solutions, preferably Nozomi Networks or comparable platforms such as Claroty or Dragos

  • Comfortable working in both office and plant environments, including regular travel to production sites

  • Professional proficiency in English

Nice-to-haves:

  • Certifications such as Fortinet FCP (NSE 4+), Palo Alto Networks PCNSE, Cisco CCNP, Nozomi Networks, IEC 62443, or GICSP

  • Experience within the process industry, energy, chemicals, manufacturing, or another industrial environment

  • Familiarity with NIS2 and experience translating regulatory requirements into practical technical controls

  • Experience with zero trust network access (such as Zscaler) and Microsoft Azure networking

  • Experience integrating network and OT logs into a SIEM, preferably Microsoft Sentinel

  • Automation or scripting experience with Python or Ansible, and Git-based workflows

  • Experience working with EPC contractors or automation vendors during plant construction and commissioning

  • Dutch language skills

About SkyNRG

Since 2009, SkyNRG has been a change maker in the aviation industry. We are dedicated to supplying and producing high-integrity Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF), making sustainable aviation a reality.

Collaboration is fundamental to achieving our ambition. We nurture genuine relationships with global partners in our drive to make SAF the alternative to fossil jet fuel.

Our in-house team of SAF experts have helped over 60 airlines and corporates reduce their climate impact using the Book & Claim mechanism; the most transparent and traceable way to support aviation sustainability with real emission reductions.

Sustainability is woven into the fabric of our company. We maintain an independent Sustainability Board, which advises the company on feedstocks and provides strategic guidance on wide-ranging sustainability issues. SkyNRG operations are certified against the RSB EU RED, CORSIA, and Book & Claim standards.

At SkyNRG, you’ll find:

  • An innovation-driven culture – where big ideas turn into real impact

  • Growth opportunities – in a fast-scaling, industry-changing company

  • A collaborative team – where your ideas and expertise are valued

  • A mission that matters – leading the change in the energy transition by producing and supplying high-integrity SAF

What we offer

We offer a brand-new office in the heart of Amsterdam, designed for collaboration and creativity. Most importantly, you’ll have the opportunity to contribute to a truly game-changing green initiative, making a real impact on the aviation industry and the planet.

Besides that, we offer:

title: Reliability & Maintenance Engineer | DSL-01
description:
Please note: For this role proficiency in both Dutch and English is required.


Reliability & Maintenance Engineer | DSL-01

As Reliability & Maintenance Engineer DSL-01, you are responsible for building and continuously improving the facility's maintenance, reliability, and asset integrity framework. Reporting to the Engineering Manager, you help ensure the plant operates safely, reliably, and efficiently.

The role starts with a strong Maintenance Engineering focus. Your priority will be to help establish the maintenance and reliability foundation of DSL-01 by answering a fundamental question: "how do we maintain our assets safely, reliably, and efficiently throughout their lifecycle?"

You will translate reliability studies, equipment criticality assessments, and integrity requirements into practical maintenance plans, inspection programmes, spare parts strategies, and asset management processes.

As the facility moves into stable operations, the focus gradually shifts towards Reliability Engineering, where you will use asset health monitoring, root cause analysis, and continuous improvement to prevent failures and improve long-term asset performance.

Working closely with operations, maintenance, engineering, and external specialists, you will help reduce technical risk and improve asset reliability from day one.

You will:

  • Develop and continuously improve maintenance, inspection, and asset integrity strategies

  • Translate reliability studies, FMECA analyses, and engineering data into practical maintenance plans within the CMMS/EAM system

  • Act as owner of the asset register from a maintenance, reliability, and integrity perspective

  • Support the implementation and continuous development of the facility's CMMS/EAM system

  • Drive reliability improvements through asset health monitoring, KPI analysis, and predictive maintenance techniques

  • Lead Root Cause Analyses (RCA) and implement sustainable corrective actions

  • Monitor and improve reliability performance indicators such as MTBF, MTTR, availability, and inspection compliance

  • Support asset improvement, modification, and long-term replacement strategies throughout the asset lifecycle

Your profile

As a growing company in a rapidly evolving industry, we are looking for people who embrace change and are motivated to actively contribute to building and scaling our business. You are someone who feels comfortable in an entrepreneurial environment, takes ownership, and enjoys turning complex technical challenges into practical solutions.

You recognize yourself in the following:

Must have

  • Fluent in Dutch and English

  • Bachelor's degree in a relevant engineering discipline (i.e. electrical or mechanical)

  • 5+ years of experience in Reliability Engineering, Maintenance Engineering, Asset Integrity, or Asset Management

  • Experience with RCM, FMEA/FMECA, RCA, and maintenance strategy development

  • Experience with CMMS/EAM systems such as SAP PM, Maximo, or IFS

Preferred

  • Experience in chemical, petrochemical, energy, or other process industries like food or FMCG

  • Experience with CMMS/EAM implementation or optimisation

  • Experience with predictive maintenance and condition monitoring

  • Knowledge of ATEX, PED, and asset integrity management

About DSL-01

DSL-01 is SkyNRG’s frontrunning renewable fuels facility in Delfzijl, Netherlands. The plant will produce Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) from residual fats and greases using the HEFA (Hydrotreated Esters and Fatty Acids) pathway, with additional renewable products like butane, propane, and naphtha as by-products.

DSL-01 is the first facility in Europe dedicated entirely to SAF and its by-products. Once operational, it will produce 100,000 tonnes of SAF and 35,000 tonnes of sustainable by-products per year, cutting greenhouse gas emissions by around 80% compared to conventional jet fuel.

Construction started in 2026, with first fuel expected in 2028. The project includes the main facility, pipelines, and temporary work areas. At DSL-01, you will be part of a team building a state-of-the-art industrial plant from the ground up, contributing to a truly sustainable energy future.

Environmental and social responsibility are at the heart of DSL-01. We follow international frameworks and Dutch regulations to manage impacts on people, nature, and local communities. Safety, sustainability, and collaboration guide everything we do.

 

What we offer

As DSL-01 is still being built, many aspects of the plant, roles, and benefits are still being shaped. Our HR team is actively defining the full compensation and benefits package specifically for the Delfzijl facility. You can be assured that the final offer will be highly competitive and designed to reward your expertise, contribution, and impact as we bring this pioneering SAF plant to life.

We are committed to offering an attractive total package to ensure we attract the best talent in the market. This includes a competitive salary, performance-based incentives, and a range of benefits that support your personal and professional growth.

 

Is this you?

At DSL-01, you will work in a dynamic, innovative environment where technical curiosity, problem-solving, and teamwork are valued. You will engage with operators, engineers, and managers across disciplines, helping to bring a pioneering renewable fuels facility to life while making a real impact on the planet.

Are you ready to help build a plant from the ground up? Join a pioneering force in sustainable aviation and help create a cleaner, more sustainable future.
